## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical pump problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating without fluid cooling. All other components are in good condition and the dispersal field is dry with no surface breakout.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter is in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Component | Condition | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Effluent Pump | Good (visual) | CRITICAL -- No Load |
| Amp Draw | 1.6A measured | 22.2% of 7.2A nameplate |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | -- |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | -- |

The pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load -- the motor is spinning but no fluid is being moved. Possible causes include a dry run (no fluid at the pump intake), a broken or missing impeller, or a severed or disconnected discharge line. Running without load creates overheating risk to the motor.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no ponding, breakout, or wet spots observed during the site walk.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE:**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. The pump is running at no load (22.2% FLA). Do not continue operating the system in this condition. A qualified technician must inspect the pump intake, impeller, and discharge line to identify whether the pump is cavitating (running dry), the impeller is damaged or missing, or the discharge line is blocked or disconnected.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is repaired and verified to be operating under normal load.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is like a car engine spinning with no oil -- the motor overheats quickly and fails. The problem could be as simple as a clogged intake screen or as serious as a broken impeller inside the pump. Either way, it needs to be diagnosed and fixed right away. Do not delay on this.

### Tank Solids
Your tank is holding solids at about 23 percent of its volume, which is normal and healthy. You are not approaching a pumping threshold. Continue keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications all slow down the biological processes that keep your system working.
